title: Telangana Bans Artificial Non-Dairy Paneer for One Year After Raids
excerpt: The state's food safety authority prohibited analogue paneer sold as "paneer" from September 10, 2026, and suspended five FSSAI licences in Hyderabad after enforcement drives found unhygienic conditions and adulterated ingredients.
body:
• Telangana has banned the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of analogue (non-dairy or artificial) paneer sold as "paneer" for one year, effective September 10, 2026.
  • The order was issued by the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) under Section 30(2)(a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and notified in gazette No. 807.
  • Enforcement teams inspected 20 food establishments in Hyderabad's Kukatpally area and suspended the FSSAI licences of five outlets over hygiene violations.
  • A separate drive found units blending palm oil, glycerol monostearate, skimmed milk powder and industrial cream to mimic paneer; goods worth ₹7.19 lakh were seized.

Telangana has imposed a one-year, statewide ban on artificial and non-dairy analogue paneer being sold as "paneer," the state's food safety authority announced on Saturday. The order, effective from September 10, 2026, prohibits the manufacture, processing, packing, storage, distribution and sale of non-dairy, artificial or analogue paneer in any form across the state.

The prohibition was issued by the Commissioner of Food Safety, Telangana State, in exercise of powers under clause (a) of sub-section (2) of Section 30 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and notified in the official gazette bearing No. 807 dated September 10, 2026. It follows a series of enforcement drives in Hyderabad targeting units making fake paneer with non-dairy ingredients.

The enforcement drives

Earlier this week, the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) ran a special enforcement drive in Hyderabad's Kukatpally area. Ten teams comprising Food Safety Officers and police personnel inspected 20 food establishments — restaurants, bakeries, sweet shops and hostels — and suspended the FSSAI licences of five establishments over food safety and hygiene violations.

According to the Commissioner's press note, inspectors found spoiled and contaminated meat and vegetables, cockroach, housefly and rodent infestation, unhygienic premises, expired food articles, improperly maintained refrigerators and records, improper segregation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, and food handlers failing to meet hygiene standards.

A separate intensive drive, reported by eDairy News India, saw 12 enforcement teams inspect 14 dairy manufacturing and retail units in Hyderabad's Core Urban Region and adjoining districts. The licences of three commercial dairy processing units were suspended and their operations halted. Officers seized adulterated and non-compliant goods valued at ₹7.19 lakh — including approximately one metric ton of loose palm oil, 476 kg of glycerol monostearate, 1,760 packs of industrial cooking cream and 150 kg of skimmed milk powder — and lifted 21 samples for laboratory testing.

What analogue paneer is

Analogue paneer is a non-dairy product designed to resemble traditional paneer in texture and appearance. Instead of milk constituents, such products may use non-dairy ingredients — vegetable fats such as palm oil, emulsifiers and starches — to replicate the characteristics of the original at far lower production costs.

The concern for consumers, as Hyderabad authorities have flagged, is nutritional: a product sold as paneer may not carry the same protein and nutrient composition as conventional dairy paneer, a significant matter in a state where paneer is a staple protein source for vegetarians.

A widening crackdown

Telangana joins Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh in moving against artificial dairy substitutes that exploit consumer trust. The state's action comes amid a national enforcement wave against fake paneer, with food safety agencies stepping up inspections at hotels, restaurants, cloud kitchens and dairy supply facilities. Officials in Telangana said regular inspections would continue, and businesses violating the order face legal penalties, confiscation of prohibited products and revocation of licences.

For the diaspora

The crackdown is a useful reminder for diaspora shoppers too: paneer sold in Indian grocery stores abroad is not subject to these inspections, so it is worth checking ingredient labels — genuine paneer lists milk and an acidulant such as lemon juice or vinegar, while substitutes rely on vegetable oils and emulsifiers. For families visiting Telangana, the ban means restaurant and sweet-shop paneer faces closer scrutiny than it has in years.

What's next

The prohibition remains in force for one year from September 10, 2026. Watch for the laboratory results from the 21 seized samples, further licence actions as TG SAFE continues its drives, and whether other states follow Telangana with their own formal bans.
